result.title: EA-Bench: Measuring information and action efficiency under imperfect instructions
result.summary: Personal agents help users complete everyday work across digital applications. Many standard benchmarks assume that users provide sufficient information to solve a task. However, agents often encounter incomplete, distracting, or inconsistent information in practice. To systematically study agent inefficiency under such imperfect information, we introduce Efficient Action (EA)-Bench, which evaluates both tool calls and user interactions in work-related tasks. To our knowledge, it is the first benchmark to jointly evaluate tool-call efficiency and user-interaction efficiency under controlled missing, redundant, and conflicting information. We construct 63 base-task instances adapted from existing work-related benchmarks. To guide perturbation design and quantify task requirements, we represent workflows as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) and examine node-level dependencies to identify where information can be withheld, contradicted, or supplemented with distractors. We use a two-stage validation process combining AI-assisted checks with expert screening to select 232 conditions from 792 initial candidates. We organize these tasks into Easy and Hard tracks by task complexity. Experiments show that imperfect information can reduce accuracy and increase tool-use and user-interaction costs. More concerning, several models obtain apparently correct outcomes by guessing user-specific values without confirmation, revealing potential execution unreliability in current models under imperfect user information.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EA-Bench，用 DAG 刻画工作流并在节点依赖处注入缺失、冗余或冲突信息，联合评测个人 agent 的准确率、工具调用效率与用户交互效率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按依赖结构受控制造信息缺口、并把交互开销与正确性分开衡量的做法，可能为 LVR 构建证据不足或相互冲突的输入、评估 LOOK 与 STOP 的收益成本提供线索，可供核查任务与指标能否迁移。
